pairs.before: Claude Haiku 5.5 is priced by prompt length: a request whose prompt is over 100,000 tokens pays higher prices. A request's prompt length counts all of its input tokens, including cache reads and cache writes. Each request is priced on its own: a request over the threshold pays the higher prices even when part of its prompt is a cache hit, and earlier requests keep the prices they were billed at. Model pricing and Batch processing list both sets of prices.

pairs.before: Claude Platform on AWS bills through AWS Marketplace using Claude Consumption Units (CCUs). Your AWS bill shows a single CCU line item.

added_lines: A 1-hour coding session using Claude Opus 5.5 that consumes 50,000 input tokens and 15,000 output tokens:
Academic and research discounts might be available
Each organization receives 1,550 free hours of usage per month.
Execution time has a minimum of 5 minutes.
If files are included in the request, execution time is billed even if the tool is not called, because files are preloaded onto the container.
Implement prompt caching: Reduce costs for repeated context.
Monitor usage patterns: Track token consumption to identify optimization opportunities.
Prompt caching multipliers apply on top of fast mode pricing.

Regional and multi-region endpoints include a 10 percent premium over global endpoints. The Claude API (first-party) is global by default; for first-party data residency options and pricing, see Data residency pricing.
The Batch API allows asynchronous processing of large volumes of requests with a 50 percent discount on both input and output tokens.
Usage tracking available in the Claude Console at platform.claude.com
Use appropriate models: Choose Haiku for simple tasks, Sonnet for most production workloads, and Opus for the most complex reasoning.
Volume discounts might be available for high-volume users. These are negotiated on a case-by-case basis.

Web search is available on the Claude API for $10 USD per 1,000 searches, plus standard token costs for search-generated content. Web search results retrieved throughout a conversation are counted as input tokens, in search iterations executed during a single turn and in subsequent conversation turns.
